newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU leaves validity period for wheat unchanged.
newsitem.headline: EU leaves validity period for wheat unchanged.

text.p: The European Union on Thursday did not cut the validity period for soft wheat export licences, grain officials said.

There had been speculation the European Commission would consider cutting the validity of licences to June 30 to prevent any newly issued export certificates being used against new crop wheat in late July or August.

But that option was sidelined when the Commission decided to stop issuing weekly licences for old-crop wheat altogether. It cannot legally change the validity period of licences already in the market.
"It was impossible to change," one official said.
Most EU licences are valid for the current month plus four months.
The only licences now available are short validity ones issued through the daily bidding system. They run for one month and have no prefixable value.
Although they carry neither a subsidy nor a tax, the Commission can introduce either before the day of loading. It can also reject bids within three working days.
